title: Annotatio V §.XII (1): Calixtus Senior — authority stands; Jud. Controv. n.76 union
pass_a_gloss: (1.) Of CALIXTUS Senior, whose man’s authority he is content merely to diminish, though among all good and moderate men, and students of ecclesiastical antiquity, it will endure — even if not infallible, nor to be held by us chiefly on that name, because he summons into one Christian Church society Pontificians no less (Trent safe though anathematizing many Protestant things) than the Reformed (Dort safe though obliquely disapproving certain Lutheran dogmas through the Arminians’ side, yet striking with no anathema). Meanwhile to this man’s unshaken testimony against Oral Eating’s Fundamentality is to be added also that by which he proves the Protestant dissension about it can in no way hinder Protestant ecclesiastical Union — because the Reformed who eat Christ’s Body spiritually eat it no less orally than the Lutherans themselves, since Oral Eating’s truth depends not on the eaters’ Opinion but on the Will of the Supper’s Institution. Jud. de Controver. n. 76.
pass_b_english: (1) Calixtus Senior: the Author only tries to shrink his authority; among moderate antiquity-minded readers it still stands — even if not infallible, and not mainly because he beckons Papists and Reformed into one church society without Dort anathemas on Lutheran dogmas.

Add also Calixtus’s point (Jud. Controv. n.76): Protestant split over Oral does not block union — Reformed who eat spiritually also eat orally if Oral truth hangs on the institution’s will, not the eaters’ opinion.
source_text: (1.) CALIXTI Senioris, cujus Viri Autoritatem dumtaxat imminuere satagit, apud omnes interim bonos moderatosque, antiquitatis item Ecclesiasticæ studiosos, perduraturam, etiamsi non infallibilis, nec à nobis, istô potissimum nomine, habenda sit, quòd Pontificios non minus, salvô licet Tridentino Concilio, Protestantica multa anathematizante, quàm Reformatos, salva horum Synodo Dordracenâ, dogmata quædam Lutherana obliquè quidem & per latus Arminianorum improbante, nullo verò anathemate feriente, in unius Ecclesiæ Christianæ Societatem advocat. Testimonio intereà hujus Viri contra Fundamentalitatem Oralis Manducationis inconcusso persistenti superaddendum & illud est, quô idem dissidium de ea Protestanticum, Unioni Protestantium Ecclesiasticæ nihil quicquam officere posse, inde probat, quòd Spiritualiter Corpus Christi manducantes Reformati, non minus Oraliter id manducent, quàm ipsi Lutherani, cùm Oralis Manducationis veritas, non à Manducantium Opinione, sed à Voluntate Institutionis Cœnæ, dependeat. Jud. de Controver. n. 76.
